Digits sum to 13 and x − y = 3 gives x = 8, y = 5, so the number is 85 (not 74, since 7+4 = 11, not 13). Check: 85 − 58 = 27 and 8+5 = 13. The sum is 85 + 58 = 143.

The solution's pair list was also wrong, since it omitted (8,5) and claimed (7,4) satisfies the sum condition. Its answer of 121 is incorrect.

Note that the sum of the number and its reverse is 11(x+y) = 11·13 = 143, which confirms this.

The correct answer is 143. With digits a and b, a + b = 13 and 9(a − b) = 27 give a − b = 3, so a = 8, b = 5. The number is 85, its reverse is 58, and 85 − 58 = 27. The sum is 85 + 58 = 143, which also equals 11·13.

Solution 2 makes algebra errors. Substituting b = 13 − a into 10a + b − (10b + a) = 27 gives 9a − 9(13 − a) = 18a − 117 = 27, so a = 8. The solution instead got −9a − 117, which is wrong. It then accepted a = 10 as a "valid digit", which it is not, and produced the non-two-digit number 103. Its answer of 134 is incorrect.
